idiom_name: JPA @Entity/@Table mapping + EntityManager (unit of work, identity map, lazy loading)
implementation_notes: The Jakarta Persistence API plus Hibernate is the canonical Java data mapper: entity classes are mapped to tables by annotations or an orm.xml descriptor, and the EntityManager supplies the identity map, change tracking and flush-in-transaction semantics, so application code loads aggregates and mutates them without seeing SQL. Hibernate's user guide documents both annotation and external-descriptor mapping, which lets a team keep the domain classes annotation-free. Domain behaviour stays in the entity while all schema knowledge lives in the mapping metadata - the persistence framework, not the model, owns the translation.
pitfalls: Lazy associations touched outside the persistence context throw LazyInitializationException; the mapper's transaction must enclose the whole load-and-use step or the fetch plan must be explicit.
Proxies for lazy loading subclass the entity, so getClass() comparisons and equals/hashCode over all fields behave surprisingly - use a business-key equals and instanceof.
A JPA entity needs a no-arg constructor and non-final fields/classes (or bytecode enhancement), a real constraint on how the domain type may be written.
Detached entities reassembled with merge() can overwrite concurrent changes: without a Version Number column, lost updates are the default failure mode.

variants.name: Spring JdbcTemplate with hand-written RowMapper
variants.implementation_notes: The classic JDBC-level mapper in Java: a RowMapper implementation turns one ResultSet row into a domain object and JdbcTemplate executes the statement, translating SQLExceptions and handling resource release. Domain classes stay annotation-free and there is no proxy or lazy-loading machinery - the mapping is exactly the code you wrote. You give up identity map, change tracking and relationship loading, so pair it with explicit transaction handling (TransactionTemplate) and hand-written collection queries where needed.
pitfalls: Column lookups by label are case- and alias-sensitive, and a missing column is an SQLException at mapping time rather than a compile error - keep the SELECT list and the mapper in one file.
Without an identity map, a one-to-many join naively mapped by RowMapper produces duplicate parent objects; use a ResultSetExtractor to assemble the graph.
JdbcTemplate hides connection acquisition, so transaction boundaries live in the service layer: a mapper called outside a transaction gets its own connection per statement.
